prompt: What single cause do lesson 3's summary-table leak and lesson 5's skew share?

choices.text: A feature computed badly
choices.why: Right. Computed in two places, or for the wrong moment; a feature store is built to prevent both.

choices.text: Both used logistic regression
choices.why: Any algorithm would have failed the same way.

choices.text: Both trained on too few members to be stable
choices.why: Both had thousands of rows; size was not the issue.

choices.text: Both forgot to scale the numeric columns
choices.why: The pipeline scaled them both times.

prompt: Does a feature store compute the features?

choices.text: Yes, it replaces features.py
choices.why: features.py still does the computing.

choices.text: No: it runs, keeps and serves the code's output
choices.why: Right. The computation stays in one piece of code.

choices.text: Only for the online store
choices.why: The online store is built from the offline one; neither computes.

choices.text: Only when the model asks for a feature it has never seen
choices.why: Nothing is computed on demand here.

prompt: Match each part of a feature store to what it is in this lesson.
Why does the event timestamp matter more than anything else in the store?

choices.text: It makes the online store faster
choices.why: Speed comes from the index, not the timestamp.

choices.text: It is the key the model is trained on
choices.why: The model never sees a date.

choices.text: It makes the table a history
choices.why: Right. Without it the store is lesson 3's summary table.

choices.text: It decides which members are active
choices.why: features.py decides that, as of each day.

prompt: Why does snapshot drop the lapsed column before writing?

choices.text: It is too large to store
choices.why: It is one small number per row.

choices.text: SQLite cannot store booleans
choices.why: It stores 0 and 1 happily.

choices.text: The online store has no room for it
choices.why: Room is not the reason.

choices.text: It is learned after the day
choices.why: Right. The store keeps what was known on the day; a label kept beside features is a leak waiting for a query.

prompt: historical uses merge_asof with direction="backward" and a tolerance of seven days. What would direction="nearest" do?

choices.text: Pick later snapshots too
choices.why: Right. A Thursday question would get the following Sunday's values.

choices.text: Nothing different, since snapshots are weekly
choices.why: A nearer snapshot after the moment would now be chosen.

choices.text: Make the join faster
choices.why: Speed is not what direction changes.

choices.text: Drop every member who has no snapshot that day
choices.why: It would find more matches, not fewer.

prompt: How many weekly snapshots did the backfill from 2025-06-01 to 2026-02-22 take?
Why is a backfill only correct because features.py computes as of its cutoff?

choices.text: Because the backfill runs faster that way
choices.why: Correctness, not speed, is the point.

choices.text: So the past is not refilled from today
choices.why: Right. From a summary table, the past would be filled with today's values.

choices.text: Because the offline store refuses rows from the past
choices.why: It accepts any day it is given.

choices.text: Because labels are computed during the backfill
choices.why: Labels are dropped before anything is stored.

prompt: A team wants training rows for any day of the past, not only Sundays. What does that cost?

choices.text: Nothing, merge_asof already handles any day
choices.why: It handles any day, with up to six days of staleness.

choices.text: A different algorithm for the lapse model
choices.why: The model is unaffected.

choices.text: Seven times the rows
choices.why: Right. Cadence is how stale a training row may be, bought with storage.

choices.text: Dropping the online store
choices.why: The two are independent.

prompt: Asked about member 2 on Thursday 27 November, which snapshot answers?

choices.text: Sunday 30 November, the nearest
choices.why: That is after the moment, so it is never used.

choices.text: Saturday 28 February, the newest in the store
choices.why: That is the summary-table mistake.

choices.text: None: there is no snapshot on that day
choices.why: The as-of join takes the latest before it.

choices.text: Sunday 23 November
choices.why: Right. The newest on or before the moment, four days stale.

prompt: What recency did the store give for member 2 as of 2025-11-27?
How is the staleness on the Thursday different from a leak?

choices.text: It is known, and bounded by MAX_AGE
choices.why: Right. At most six days, written as MAX_AGE; a leak has no bound and no name.

choices.text: It is not different; both read the wrong day
choices.why: Staleness reads an earlier day, which was knowable then.

choices.text: Staleness only happens online
choices.why: It happened here in a historical join.

choices.text: A leak is always smaller
choices.why: Lesson 3's was large enough to take AUC to 0.994.

choices.text: SQLite has a limit on rows per table
choices.why: Not one this store comes near.

choices.text: Crash, so somebody notices

prompt: Why is features.build a poor way to answer for one member in a web request?

choices.text: It returns the label as well
choices.why: True, but the problem in a request is time.

choices.text: It cannot read SQLite from a web server
choices.why: It can; it is just slow for one member.

choices.text: It uses a different scaler
choices.why: Scaling is inside the model, not in features.build.

choices.text: It computes all of them each time
choices.why: Right. It computes every active member to answer one, because it was written for training.

prompt: lookup.py prints 0.17 ms on one run and 0.15 ms on another. What should a reader take from the numbers?

choices.text: That the online store got faster
choices.why: Run-to-run noise, not a change.

choices.text: That SQLite is the right online store for any size

choices.text: That the timing is wrong, since it changed
choices.why: Timings always vary a little; that is not an error.

prompt: A colleague builds a training set by joining labels to a nightly members summary with no as_of column. Which part of a feature store would have prevented it?

choices.text: Event timestamps and the point-in-time join
choices.why: Right. Without them, today's values meet last year's labels.

choices.text: The online store's index
choices.why: Indexes make it fast, not correct.

choices.text: The time to live
choices.why: It would hide stale rows, not stop the future joining the past.

choices.text: A registry of owners
choices.why: Knowing the owner does not change the join.
